long_biography.plain_text:
Yazdi trained as an engineer and began his career managing software projects before pursuing his own digital-products business. After a period as a professional poker player, he reunited with school friend Laurent Ritter to create consumer mobile products. Their first game failed, but the setback persuaded them to replace long development cycles with rapid experiments measured against real user behaviour.

That method produced Paper.io and became Voodoo's publishing model: prototype quickly, discard weak concepts and share revenue with independent studios whose games could scale. Yazdi later guided the company beyond advertising-funded hyper-casual titles into deeper casual games and consumer apps, including BeReal, while continuing as co-founder and chief executive.
